observations: The current source defines and registers chair_body, but the evaluated chair-body mesh is unavailable, so all rendered views show only the four legs and generated tabs.

The evaluator reports three zero-area triangles in generated hull geometry_0_hull.001. Source construction order makes SeatShell.__init__.front_roll—the second rounded_box hull—the strongest initial localization candidate, but the generated node name does not prove unique ownership.

Each leg has the same OPEN_PRINT_MESH pattern: 12 boundary edges localized to part-local z=327–330 mm. This exactly coincides with the final 3 mm of the generated tab because leg_tab_frame starts at z=300 mm, insertion_mm is 30 mm, and shared_leg_mount.lead_in_mm is 3 mm.

Assembly standing is unverified because rigid print meshes are unavailable; this is not evidence that the chair is unstable. The Dapper partition score is also unavailable, so no print regrouping is supported in this round.
The four connection frames, 0.2 mm fit allowance, leg placements, root part, and reported overall envelope do not have independent evidence of error and should remain unchanged.
required_changes: Apply one bounded source patch: reconstruct only SeatShell.__init__.front_roll without its single eight-sphere hull, and remove the 3 mm generated tab lead-in shared by the four otherwise unchanged leg connectors. Preserve the front-roll envelope, upholstery appearance, all connector frame locations, insertion depth, tab section, frozen fit allowance, chair hierarchy, symmetry, and 900 × 800 × 900 mm overall bounds. Re-export and re-run every configured checker and appearance review.
checker_interpretation: The chair-body display failure and zero-area-triangle diagnostic support replacing the localized front_roll hull construction with overlapping positive-volume primitives; they do not support redesigning the complete upholstered body.

The identical leg boundary regions at z=327–330 mm align specifically with shared_leg_mount.lead_in_mm=3.0 at the tops of tabs extending from z=300 to z=330 mm. Setting only that lead-in to zero is a falsifiable local source repair attempt; the OPEN_PRINT_MESH cause remains unconfirmed until re-export.

assembly_standing and assembly_overhang are dependency-blocked measurements. They must be rerun after mesh export is restored and cannot presently be treated as PASS or as independent physical failures.

repair_proposals.hypothesis: The four open leg meshes originate in the shared 3 mm tapered lead-in at the generated tab tips, while the missing chair body originates in the second rounded_box hull used for SeatShell.__init__.front_roll. Replacing that one hull with an equivalent overlapping-solid construction and setting only shared_leg_mount.lead_in_mm to zero should produce closed printable meshes without moving interfaces or changing the visible chair envelope.
evidence: All four leg findings report the same 12 open boundary edges in part-local bounds x/y within ±19 mm and z=327–330 mm.
The connector tab is centered at z=300 mm, has insertion_mm=30.0, and has lead_in_mm=3.0, placing its lead-in precisely in the measured z=327–330 mm region.
The current source creates all four affected tabs from the same shared_leg_mount TabSlot object, explaining the repeated boundary pattern.
The evaluator reports EVALUATED_MESH_DEGENERATE with three zero-area triangles in geometry_0_hull.001.

rounded_box returns one hull over eight spheres, and SeatShell.__init__.front_roll is the second rounded_box construction in source order, making it a bounded initial candidate rather than a proven unique cause.
Resolved visual feedback requires restoration of chair_body while preserving its hierarchy, bounds, symmetry, and four slot interfaces.

front_roll.implementation: Replace only this rounded_box hull with a boolean union of overlapping positive-volume center slabs and corner/edge primitives; do not alter its exact AABB.
